q: Which of these is a LIQUID?
e: Juice flows and takes the shape of its container, so it is a liquid.

q: Which of these is a SOLID?
e: A ball keeps its own shape, so it is a solid.

q: A rubber band can bend and stretch without breaking. What property does it have?
e: Flexible means it can bend easily.

q: Which object is NOT flexible?
e: A glass jar is stiff and does not bend.

q: A cup of hot cocoa and a glass of ice water are compared. What property is different?
e: Hot and cold tell the temperature of each drink.

q: Which group has only liquids?
e: Water, milk, and juice all flow.

q: A student sorts materials into groups called ROUGH and SMOOTH. Which property is used?
e: Rough and smooth describe how a surface feels.

q: A student folds a flat sheet of paper into a boat. What property changed?
e: Folding changes the shape but the paper is still paper.

q: A student cuts a sheet of paper into small pieces. What stayed the same?
e: The pieces are still paper.

q: A student sands a rough block of wood. How does the block feel after?
e: Sanding makes a surface smoother.

q: Juice is poured into a mold and placed in a freezer. What does it become?
o: a new kind of juice that is hotter
e: Freezing makes a liquid turn into a solid.

q: A crayon is held near a flame and gets soft and runny. Which process caused this?
e: Heat makes wax melt.

q: A student wants to make a piece of clay flat. What can the student do?
e: Pressing changes the clay's shape.

q: A student tears a paper, folds it, then cuts it. Which is still true about the pieces?
e: Cutting, folding, and tearing change shape or size, not the material.

q: Building blocks can be put together to make what?
e: Small units can be combined in many ways to make new objects.

q: A student takes apart a block tower and builds a bridge with the same blocks. What does this show?
e: Small units can be reassembled into new objects.

q: Which material is best for building a bridge that holds weight?
e: A bridge needs a strong, stiff material.

q: Why is a raincoat made of waterproof plastic?
e: The material is chosen because water does not go through it.

q: Which material is best for a soft pillow?
e: Cotton is soft and comfortable.

q: A toy boat needs to float. Which material is best?
e: Foam is light and floats on water.

q: A student builds a tall tower with blocks. Which choice would help make it stronger?
o: use a wide base of blocks
use only one block at the bottom
make it lean to one side
e: A wide base makes a tower more stable.

q: A ball hits a wall. What does the wall do to the ball?
e: When objects touch, they push on each other.

q: A student presses a sponge with a hand. What happens to the sponge?
e: A push can change an object's shape.

q: Two bumper cars hit each other. What happens?
o: they push on each other and move
e: Colliding objects push on each other.

q: A soft clay ball is dropped on the floor. What may happen to the ball?
e: The push from the floor can change the clay's shape.

q: A hammer hits a nail. Which describes the push?
o: the hammer pushes the nail and the nail pushes back
e: When objects touch, each pushes on the other.

q: A student squeezes a rubber ball. What happens when the student lets go?
o: it goes back to its shape
e: A rubber ball can spring back after being squeezed.

q: Which collision is most likely to change an object's shape?
o: a leaf landing on a pillow
a feather landing on a rock
a truck crashing into a soft sandcastle
e: A strong collision with a soft object changes its shape.

q: A stronger push on a toy car makes the car move how?
e: A stronger push makes the car move faster.

q: A student pushes a ball gently and then pushes it hard. How does the motion change?
o: the hard push makes it go farther
the gentle push makes it go farther
e: A harder push makes it travel farther.

q: A student pulls a wagon with a weak pull and a strong pull. Which makes the wagon speed up more?
e: A stronger pull changes the motion more.

q: A student wants to test how push strength affects a car. What should change in the test?
o: how hard the car is pushed
e: To test the push, only the strength of the push should change.

q: A student measures how far a ball rolls after a soft push. What tool measures the distance?
e: A measuring tape measures length.

q: A swing is pushed lightly and then pushed hard. Which swing goes higher?
e: A harder push makes a swing go higher.

q: A student records: soft push = 20 cm, medium push = 45 cm, hard push = 80 cm. What does the data show?
o: a stronger push makes the object travel farther
e: As the push gets stronger, the distance gets longer.

q: What makes sound?
e: Sound is made when matter vibrates, or moves back and forth quickly.

q: A student plucks a rubber band and it moves quickly back and forth. What does the student hear?
e: The vibrating rubber band makes sound.

q: A drum is hit and rice on top of the drum jumps. What does the rice show?
e: The jumping rice shows the drum skin vibrates.

q: A student puts a hand on their throat while humming. What does the hand feel?
e: The vocal cords vibrate when a person hums.

q: When a tuning fork stops vibrating, what happens to its sound?
e: No vibration means no sound.

q: Which can cause vibrations that make sound?
e: Many actions cause vibrations.

q: A loud sound can make a window rattle. What does this show?
o: sound can cause other things to vibrate
e: Vibrations from sound can make other objects vibrate.

q: Which sound is the QUIETEST?
e: A whisper is a very soft sound.

q: Why does a fire alarm make a very loud sound?
o: to be heard by no one
e: A loud alarm gets people's attention.

q: A teacher uses a soft voice in the library. Why?
e: Soft sounds help keep a place quiet.

q: Which place needs a quiet sound level?
e: A library is a place for quiet reading.

q: Which sound is LOUD?
e: Thunder is a very loud sound.

q: A bus driver honks a horn to warn a car. Why is the horn loud?
o: so the other driver can hear it
e: A loud horn is meant to be heard quickly.

q: Which is the BEST sound level for a doctor speaking to a patient in a quiet room?
e: A calm, soft voice is best for talking in a quiet room.

q: Two cups and a string can be used to make a simple device. What can it help people do?
e: A string telephone carries vibrations from one cup to the other.

q: In a cup-and-string phone, what carries the sound from one cup to the other?
e: The string vibrates and carries the sound.

q: For a cup-and-string phone to work well, the string should be what?
e: A tight string carries vibrations better.

q: Which tool helps a person call to others across a field?
e: A megaphone makes a voice louder so it travels farther.

q: A student builds a sound device and it is too quiet. What can be changed?
e: A tighter string helps vibrations travel.

q: Which problem can a sound device help solve?
o: talking to a friend across a playground
e: Sound devices help people communicate over a distance.

q: A student's cup-and-string phone does not work. The string is touching a pole. What is the likely problem?
o: the string is too short to hear
the string is not able to vibrate freely
e: A string touching something cannot vibrate well.

q: The Sun is what kind of object?
e: The Sun is a star that gives off light and heat.

q: What does the Sun give to Earth?
e: The Sun provides light and heat.

q: Why can we see the Moon at night?
o: it reflects light from the Sun
e: The Moon reflects the Sun's light.

q: Which sky object produces its own light?
e: The Sun is a star that makes its own light.

q: Which is closest to Earth?
e: The Moon is much closer to Earth than the Sun or other stars.

q: A mirror reflects a flashlight's light onto a wall. Which sky object works like the mirror?
e: The Moon reflects sunlight like a mirror.

q: The Sun looks much bigger than other stars at night. Why?
o: it is much closer to Earth
e: The Sun is a star that is very close compared to other stars.

q: Which tool helps you see faraway objects in the sky?
e: A telescope makes faraway things look closer.

q: Compared with eyes alone, a telescope makes the Moon look how?
e: A telescope shows more detail.

q: Why do stars look like tiny dots without a tool?
o: they are very small and close
e: Stars are so far away that they look like tiny points.

q: A student sees craters on the Moon using a tool. Which tool was used?
e: Craters are easy to see with a telescope.

q: Which should you NEVER look at directly, even with a tool, unless you have special protection?
e: Looking at the Sun can hurt your eyes.

q: Binoculars help you see the night sky how?
e: Binoculars gather light and magnify.

q: A student draws the Moon as seen by eyes alone and by telescope. What would be different?
o: the telescope drawing shows no Moon
the telescope drawing has more detail
the eye drawing has more detail
e: A telescope reveals more details.

q: What can wind do to sand on a beach?
e: Wind can pile up sand into dunes.

q: What can a river do to rocks?
e: Moving water carries rocks and sand.

q: After a storm, a pile of dirt at the bottom of a hill is bigger. What most likely moved the dirt?
e: Water can wash soil downhill.

q: Which landform can be made by wind blowing sand?
e: Wind blowing sand can build dunes.

q: Strong wind in a dry place can move what?
e: Wind can carry small, light particles.

q: A fast river carries more rocks than a slow river. Why?
e: Faster water can move larger and more particles.

q: Which two things move soil and rock from one place to another?
e: Wind and water both carry particles to new places.

q: Which tool measures temperature?
e: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the air is.

q: Which tool measures how much rain falls?
e: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall.

q: A bar graph shows rain each day: Mon 2 cm, Tue 0 cm, Wed 5 cm. Which day was the rainiest?
e: Wednesday had the tallest bar, 5 cm.

q: A student records the temperature every day at noon for a week. Why?
o: to find patterns in the weather
e: Recording data over time shows patterns.

q: A thermometer shows 90°F. What kind of day is it?
e: 90°F is hot weather.

q: Precipitation includes which of these?
e: Rain, snow, sleet, and hail are precipitation.

q: Temperatures for four days are 70, 72, 75, 78. What pattern do you see?
e: Each day is a little warmer.

q: Which severe weather event has a spinning funnel of wind?
e: A tornado is a spinning funnel of strong wind.

q: A hurricane forms over what?
e: Hurricanes form over warm ocean water.

q: What is a flood?
o: too much water covering dry land
e: A flood happens when water covers land that is usually dry.

q: Which place is MORE likely to have hurricanes?
o: a coast near a warm ocean
e: Hurricanes happen near warm ocean coasts.

q: A severe storm warning is announced. What should people do?
e: Staying safe during severe weather is the best choice.

q: Which severe weather is MORE likely in a very cold place?
e: Blizzards happen where it is very cold and snowy.

q: Some severe weather happens more in some places than others. Why?
o: the weather picks a place at random
e: Climate and geography affect the kinds of storms in a region.

q: Which is a natural resource?
e: Water comes from nature.

q: Which is MANMADE?
e: People make plastic bottles.

q: A wooden table is made from what natural resource?
e: Wood comes from trees.

q: Which group has only natural resources?
e: Air, water, and sunlight come from nature.

q: Paper is made from what?
e: Paper comes from wood pulp from trees.

q: Which is a manmade object?
e: A bicycle is made by people.

q: Glass is made by melting a natural material found on beaches. Which natural resource is it?
e: Sand comes from nature, and people melt it to make glass.

q: Which is a way to REUSE something?
o: use an old jar to hold pencils
throw the jar in a stream
e: Reusing means using something again.

q: Which is a way to RECYCLE?
o: put a plastic bottle in a recycling bin
e: Recycling means turning used materials into new things.

q: Which choice helps REDUCE trash?
o: buy a new plastic bottle every day
e: Using a reusable bottle makes less trash.

q: Where should a used soda can go?
e: Metal cans can be recycled.

q: Why is it good to recycle paper?
e: Recycling paper means fewer trees are cut down.

q: A student uses both sides of a piece of paper. What is this?
e: Using both sides uses less paper.

q: Which action BEST limits harm to the environment?
o: throw all trash in one bin
e: Reduce, reuse, and recycle lower the harm people cause.

q: A desert gets very little rain. Which plant can live there?
e: A cactus stores water and needs little rain.

q: A rainforest gets a lot of rain. What does this help grow?
e: A lot of rain supports many kinds of plants.

q: Why do fewer animals live in a very dry desert?
o: there is little water and food
e: Animals need water and food.

q: A pond dries up in summer. What happens to the frogs that live there?
e: Animals need water to survive.

q: Which environment has the most rainfall?
e: Rainforests get a lot of rain each year.

q: Polar bears live where it is very cold. What helps them live there?
e: Thick fur and fat keep polar bears warm.

q: A camel lives in a desert. Which fact helps it live there?
o: it needs a pond every day
it can go a long time without water
e: Camels are adapted for a dry place.

q: What is a PRODUCER in a food chain?
o: a living thing that makes its own food
an animal that eats other animals
e: Plants are producers that make their own food.

q: What is a CONSUMER?
o: a living thing that eats other living things
a plant that makes food from sunlight
e: Consumers cannot make their own food, so they eat other living things.

q: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, which kind of living thing is the producer?
e: Grass is a plant, and plants make their own food from sunlight.

q: Algae are tiny plant-like living things in water. A small fish eats the algae. What does the small fish get from eating them?
e: Animals get energy from the food they eat.

q: A caterpillar eats leaves. A bird eats the caterpillar. Which is a consumer?
e: Both animals are consumers.

q: Which animal eats ONLY plants?
e: A rabbit eats plants only.

q: If all the grass in a field died, what would happen to the rabbits?
e: Rabbits depend on grass for food.

q: A bee flies from flower to flower. What is the bee helping the flowers do?
e: Bees carry pollen, which helps flowers make seeds.

q: Dandelion seeds float away on the wind. What does the wind do?
e: Wind moves seeds to new places.

q: A squirrel buries acorns and forgets some. What may happen?
e: Forgotten seeds can grow into new trees.

q: Some seeds have hooks that stick to fur. How does this help the plant?
o: the seeds stay in one place
an animal carries the seeds away
e: Hooks catch on animals and travel to new places.

q: A coconut falls into the ocean and floats to another island. What moved the seed?
e: Water can carry seeds to new places.

q: A hummingbird drinks nectar from a flower. What does it help the flower do?
e: Hummingbirds carry pollen between flowers.

q: Why do plants need to spread their seeds far from the parent plant?
o: to have enough space, water, and light
e: Seeds that grow too close compete for resources.

q: What do roots do for a plant?
o: take in water and hold it in the soil
e: Roots anchor a plant and take in water.

q: What do leaves do for a plant?
o: carry water from the ground only
hold the plant in the ground
e: Leaves use sunlight to make food.

q: Which plant part helps a plant stand up and carries water to the leaves?
e: The stem holds the plant up and moves water.

q: Which plant part makes seeds?
e: Flowers make the seeds.

q: A cactus has thick stems. How does this help it?
e: A thick stem holds water for dry times.

q: A fruit protects what part of a plant?
e: Fruit covers the seeds.

q: A water lily has leaves that float. How does this help it?
o: it can get sunlight at the water's surface
it can grow roots in the air
e: Floating leaves get sunlight.

q: A woodpecker has a sharp beak. How does it use it?
o: to dig a burrow in sand
e: A woodpecker pecks wood to find insects.

q: A whale comes to the surface. Why?
e: Whales breathe air through lungs.

q: A fish takes in oxygen with what body part?
e: Gills take oxygen from water.

q: A bird with a long, thin beak is most likely to eat what?
e: A long thin beak fits into a flower.

q: An elephant uses its trunk to do what?
e: An elephant uses its trunk to drink and pick up food.

q: Camels store fat in a hump. How does this help them?
o: they can go a long time without food
e: The fat gives energy when food is hard to find.

q: An owl hunts at night and has big eyes. How do big eyes help?
o: it can fly faster in the day
it can see in dim light
e: Big eyes gather more light.

q: Wolves hunt in a pack. How does this help them?
e: Working together helps them catch food.

q: A herd of zebras stays together. How does this help them?
o: there are more eyes to watch for danger
e: A group watches for danger together.

q: Penguins huddle close together in cold weather. Why?
e: Huddling shares body heat.

q: A group of fish swimming together is called a what?
e: Fish that swim together are called a school.

q: Ants work together to carry food to the nest. What does this show?
e: Working as a group helps them get food.

q: Bees live in a hive. How does the hive help the bees?
o: they share work and stay safe
e: Bees share jobs in the hive.

q: When winter comes, a group of geese flies south together. What is this called?
e: Migration is moving to another place for the season.

q: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly. What is the change called?
e: Metamorphosis is a big change in body form.

q: Which shows a butterfly life cycle in order?
e: A butterfly goes from egg to caterpillar to chrysalis to adult.

q: A tadpole lives in water and has a tail. What will it become?
e: A tadpole grows into a frog.

q: How is a tadpole different from an adult frog?
o: a tadpole has four legs from birth
a tadpole has gills and a tail
a tadpole lives only on land
e: Tadpoles live in water with gills and a tail.

q: Does a caterpillar look like its parent butterfly?
e: A caterpillar looks very different from a butterfly.

q: A butterfly lays an egg on a leaf. What hatches from the egg?
e: A caterpillar hatches from a butterfly egg.

q: Which animal has young that do NOT look like their parents?
e: A tadpole does not look like an adult frog.
